exactText: The capability overhang from the models we have today is big enough that large-scale change to work and society over the next 5+ years is now inevitable even if AI development stops. (And there is no real sign that AI development is slowing down, it appears to be accelerating)
sourceQuote: large-scale change to work and society over the next 5+ years is now inevitable even if AI development stops.
normalizedClaim: Large-scale changes to work and society from current AI capabilities are inevitable over the next 5+ years (by ~2031), even if further AI development stops.
resolutionCriteria: Observable widespread changes in job structures, productivity metrics, or organizational processes attributable to current-generation AI, documented in labor statistics (BLS), OECD reports, or major academic studies by 2031.

exactText: That work will change around AI is inevitable, but the way work changes is not. I think firms with a lack of imagination will see AI as an opportunity to cut people, but firms with the vision to expand human roles & make them better with AI will thrive.
sourceQuote: firms with a lack of imagination will see AI as an opportunity to cut people, but firms with the vision to expand human roles & make them better with AI will thrive.
normalizedClaim: Firms that use AI to expand and improve human roles will outperform those that primarily use it for headcount reduction.
resolutionCriteria: Comparative performance data (revenue growth, stock returns, or productivity metrics) of AI-adopting firms categorized by “augmentation” vs “replacement” strategies, as reported in academic studies or analyst reports by 2030.

exactText: I don’t think we know anything for certain, but I also think we are past the point where recursive self-improvement is science fiction. Instead, it is an explicit item on the roadmap of every major AI company.
sourceQuote: we are past the point where recursive self-improvement is science fiction. Instead, it is an explicit item on the roadmap of every major AI company.
normalizedClaim: Recursive self-improvement of AI is no longer science fiction and is an explicit roadmap item for major AI labs.
resolutionCriteria: Public statements, technical papers, or product roadmaps from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, or xAI explicitly listing recursive self-improvement or automated AI research as active goals, verifiable by 2027.

exactText: If the current patterns hold, the next generation of AI models should beat human experts on average in this test.
sourceQuote: the next generation of AI models should beat human experts on average in this test.
normalizedClaim: The next generation of AI models (post-2025) will outperform human experts on average on the METR long-task agentic benchmark.
resolutionCriteria: METR or equivalent independent evaluations showing frontier AI models exceeding average human expert performance on multi-hour realistic tasks by end of 2027.

exactText: Even if AI development stopped today, we would have years of change ahead of us integrating these systems into our world. ... Long before AIs achieve human-level performance, their impact on work and society will be profound and far-reaching.
sourceQuote: Even if AI development stopped today, we would have years of change ahead of us integrating these systems into our world.
normalizedClaim: Even if AI model development froze at 2024 levels, multi-year profound changes to work and society would still occur from integration of existing systems.
resolutionCriteria: Documented large-scale workplace and societal adaptations to GPT-4-class systems continuing through 2027–2028, as measured by adoption surveys (e.g., McKinsey, Pew) and labor market studies.

exactText: AI is advancing so quickly that companies should stop thinking of it as a better chatbot and start treating it as a system that can carry out hours of independent work
sourceQuote: start treating it as a system that can carry out hours of independent work
normalizedClaim: Companies should treat current AI as capable of performing hours of independent work rather than merely as improved chatbots.
resolutionCriteria: Enterprise adoption data and case studies showing AI agents routinely completing multi-hour autonomous tasks in production environments by 2028, reported by major consultancies or academic papers.

exactText: From an AI user perspective, the four big leaps so far in ability: 1. GPT-3.5 (ChatGPT, November 2022) 2. GPT-4 (Spring 2023) 3. Reasoners (starts with o1-preview, but the real deal was o3, Spring 2025) 4. Workable agentic systems (Harness + good reasoner models, December 2025)
sourceQuote: Workable agentic systems (Harness + good reasoner models, December 2025)
normalizedClaim: Workable agentic AI systems capable of reliable multi-step work emerged around December 2025.
resolutionCriteria: Public availability and demonstrated capability of agentic systems (e.g., Claude Code, OpenAI Codex/Computer Use, or equivalents) performing useful multi-hour tasks by early 2026, as documented in product releases and user reports.

resolution.explanation: Agentic systems such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and similar tools became widely available and demonstrated multi-hour independent work capability in late 2025 / early 2026.

evidence.sourceTitle: Product releases and contemporaneous reports on agentic AI

exactText: It can't just be chat bots where people ask write my essay for me or summarize this data for me. It's going to have to be a deeper form of interaction.
sourceQuote: It's going to have to be a deeper form of interaction.
normalizedClaim: Effective organizational AI use in 2026 and beyond will require deeper integration beyond simple chatbot interactions.
resolutionCriteria: Surveys and case studies of enterprise AI deployment in 2026–2028 showing majority of high-value use cases involve agentic, multi-step, or process-embedded systems rather than pure chat interfaces.

exactText: whatever AI you're using now is the worst AI you're ever going to use. Even if the core large language model development stopped right now, there's another ten years of just making it work better with tools and with industry in ways that'll continue to be disruptive.
sourceQuote: whatever AI you're using now is the worst AI you're ever going to use. Even if the core large language model development stopped right now, there's another ten years of just making it work better
normalizedClaim: Current AI (at the time of statement) will be the worst users ever experience; even frozen model progress yields a decade of disruptive tool and integration improvements.
resolutionCriteria: Continued measurable improvements in AI usefulness through tooling, agents, and integration over the subsequent 5–10 years, even in scenarios of slower base-model progress, as tracked by user studies and capability benchmarks.

exactText: Cybersecurity is going to become a mess soon
sourceQuote: Cybersecurity is going to become a mess soon
normalizedClaim: Cybersecurity challenges will escalate significantly in the near term due to advancing AI capabilities (including less-guardrailed and open models).
resolutionCriteria: Documented increase in AI-enabled cyber incidents, vulnerability disclosures, or expert consensus reports (e.g., from CISA, major security firms) describing a sharp rise in AI-related cybersecurity complexity by 2028.
